text:
marco: quick check-in — ran the length+decode-rate cohorting probe on prod-canary for 6h last night. overall P95 latency down ~6%, but seeing a small KV churn spike for short-high-decode requests.
jess: nice. which admission tweak did you run?
marco: enabled soft-admission with token_budget_target=96 for short buckets, kept decode-rate bucketing threshold at 20 tok/s. also lowered max_batch_wait to 8ms for those cohorts.
priya: did kernel-selection flip more often? iirc frequent kernel flips can cause jitter on small batches.
marco: yes, flip rate up ~3x on nodes with mixed seqs. logs show kernel handoff at around batch_effective_length ~480. small-high-decode requests occasionally join mid-batch, pushing effective_length over the kernel-flip boundary.
alex: could be our kernel boundary is too coarse. what if we move kernel flip threshold to 640 for CUDA-2080 pools?
marco: tried that in a microprobe — flip count dropped and tail smoothed at cost of ~1.5% throughput on long-only workloads. tradeoff seems acceptable for user-facing P95.
jess: KV behavior — is the churn from miss-induced prefetches?
marco: partly. short-high-decode requests have tiny prompt but high autoreg tokens; they prefetch full KV ranges then evict between batches because token budgets were low, so warmup thrash.
priya: can we bias KV retention for cohorts with high decode rate? like a small persistent slice for high-decode buckets.
alex: we have a conservative flag `kv_persistence_weight` per cohort. worth bumping for decode-heavy cohorts from 0.2 -> 0.6.
marco: i ran a trial bumping persistence to 0.55; KV miss-rate dropped ~22% and tail improved, but memory pressure rose on dense nodes.
priya: maybe combine with a smarter prefix cache: only persist last N sequence keys for short prompts. N=16 looked decent in sim.
sre-bot: alert suppressed — node mem at 83% after persistence bump; autoscaler added one extra pod to the pool.
marco: noted. on the batching classifier side, the misclassification rate for decode-rate buckets was ~8% (requests placed one bucket off). root cause: our per-request decode estimate uses a 2s EMA with alpha=0.2 which lags for bursty clients.
jess: stopgap: use a short-term window override when recent tokens/sec > 3x historical. simple rule: if instant_rate > 3x EMA then treat as high-decode for next 5s.
marco: implemented that in the probe config and re-ran for 1h — misclass down to 2.1%, no negative impact on batching.
alex: good. does this interact with admission token budget targets? short-high-decode were capped at 96, maybe bump to 128 when overridden so they don't get undersized batches.
marco: updated token_budget_target map: short/low-decode=64, short/high-decode=128 (override), long/low-decode=512, long/high-decode=512. initial runs look stable.
priya: any perf regressions on throughput or model utilization?
marco: throughput steady; GPU utilization dips a bit on nodes where we raised KV persistence due to memory pressure and more conservative batching, but overall TP50/TP95 improved for targets.
jess: can we add a small hysteresis on kernel flips to avoid flip-flop when effective_length hovers near threshold? maybe require sustained >threshold for two consecutive batches.
marco: good idea — i prototyped `kernel_flip_hold=2` batches; flip rate drops and latency tail nicer.
priya: for rollout plan: 1) deploy EMA override + token budget bump to 10% of fleet, 2) monitor KV miss, mem pressure, kernel flip rate, 3) if stable after 24h, increase to 50%, 4) then apply kernel_flip_hold globally.
alex: add perf-bot dashboards: cohort_misclass_rate, kv_miss_rate, kernel_flip_per_min, p95_latency_by_cohort, mem% by node.
marco: perf-bot posted latest probe summary ->
perf-bot: "probe-summary: cohort_misclass_rate=2.1%, p95_latency_change=-5.8%, kv_miss_rate=-22%, kernel_flips_per_min=-68% (on canary subset)."
priya: ok go for 10% canary rollout this morning. leaving a note on runbook for SRE if mem>85% or kv_miss_rate increases.
sre-bot: runbook linked: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-persistence-ooms
marco: thanks — i'll kick off canary now and update in #eng-runtime when we hit 1h/6h markers. :thumbsup:
jess: great job. small follow-up: create an E2E perf test to simulate bursty decode clients so classifier tuning survives traffic shapes.
marco: added to backlog (ticket INF-4282).
